entries: what do you do in gta online

GTA Online is GTA V's multiplayer world. You use a custom character, roam Freemode, play Jobs and Heists, buy properties and vehicles, and build different criminal businesses and activities over time.

Story Mode follows Michael, Franklin, and Trevor through a fixed campaign. GTA Online uses your own character in a persistent multiplayer sandbox with Jobs, Heists, businesses, properties, vehicles, and ongoing content updates.

GTA Online uses a custom player character rather than one of the Story Mode protagonists as your main avatar. Character appearance, clothing, hairstyles, tattoos, and other cosmetics can be changed through the game's shops and supported menus.

RP is Reputation Points. Earning RP raises your Rank, which is used by GTA Online for progression and access to some content, equipment, or older unlock conditions. Rockstar has removed some historical rank requirements over time, so current requirements can differ by feature.

GTA$ is GTA Online's in-game currency. Earnings come from Jobs, Heists, businesses, Freemode work, activities, and other content. Some systems use wallet cash while many purchases and business transactions use money held through Maze Bank.

The Player Interaction Menu is a central GTA Online menu for quick player and service controls. On official platforms the default control differs by system: PC uses M, PlayStation uses the Touchpad, and Xbox uses the View button.

GTA Online lets players choose supported spawn locations so a new session can start at a selected property or other available location. The exact choices depend on what the character owns and which content is available.

Daily Objectives are rotating tasks that reward GTA$ and RP. Rockstar has changed the objective pool and streak rewards over time, so Franklin should avoid quoting a payout from memory unless the current event notes confirm it.
Awards track accomplishments across GTA Online activities. New updates often add their own Awards, and some newer platforms also include Career Progress challenges tied to specific content.

Career Builder is an official GTA Online onboarding feature on supported newer platforms. It lets eligible players begin with one of four criminal career paths: Biker, Executive, Gunrunner, or Nightclub Owner, plus a starting budget for selected essentials.
A public session is an open GTA Online Freemode lobby where matchmaking can place multiple players together. Some Freemode events and competitive interactions are built around shared sessions.

An Invite Only session limits the Freemode lobby to players who are invited. It is useful when you want a controlled session instead of general public matchmaking, though feature availability can depend on the activity and game version.

GTA Online supports playing with friends and Crews through its session and invite systems. Crew membership is a social layer for grouping players, while individual activities can still have their own lobby and player-count requirements.
what is a crew gta online

A Crew is a Rockstar social group that players can join for shared identity and group play. Crews can be used for social organization, Crew-related matchmaking and, where supported, Crew emblems and colors.

Passive Mode reduces direct PvP interaction in Freemode. Rockstar's rules include restrictions and cooldowns, and Passive Mode cannot be active while using a weaponized vehicle. Exact timers can change with updates.

Go Ghosted is a GTA Online anti-griefing option that can temporarily make players non-interactive with a repeated attacker or their group after qualifying deaths. Rockstar has adjusted its trigger and duration over time.

GTA Online includes player-reporting and safety tools. Newer updates added a Safety and Alerts area and clearer notices around communication and reporting, while platform privacy settings can also affect social features.

User Generated Content can depend on Rockstar and platform privacy settings. If created Jobs or Crews are unavailable, check that community creations and relevant online communication permissions are enabled for the account and platform.
Jobs are instanced GTA Online activities. They include Contact Missions, Races, Deathmatches, Survivals, Adversary Modes, Heist content, and other Rockstar or player-created activities.
Contact Missions are structured missions offered by GTA Online contacts. They can involve combat, deliveries, theft, recovery, or other objectives and are separate from open Freemode business work.
Races are competitive Jobs built around checkpoints and finish order. GTA Online includes many race types and series, and Rockstar has continued adding race options and Creator features over time.
Deathmatches are combat Jobs where players or teams compete for kills or score under the selected rules. Player-created variants can also be built through supported Creator tools.

Survivals are wave-based combat Jobs where players fight repeated enemy waves. Rockstar has continued updating Survival content and removed the old rank requirement for unlocking Survivals in the Money Fronts era.
Adversary Modes are rule-driven competitive activities with specific team or objective mechanics. Rockstar rotates and adds different Adversary variants across updates and events.

Playlists group multiple Jobs into a sequence so players can continue through several activities without manually choosing each one separately.
